questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature and the chance to explore a different culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The first week was an introduction week and it was very well organized with all information you might need

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They picked me up from the airport to my accomodation and then I had recieved information about where to show up and when in relation to the intro days.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of private housing opportunities in Stellies, just make sure to start looking in advance if you want to find housing on your own! The uni has a list of accredited housing partners on their website you can reach out to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really liked my housing experience. My rent was a bit higher than if I had gotten housing through the university but my living standard was a lot higher so it was definitely worth it! I lived together with two other student, one full-time south african student and one other exchange student. My friends that stayed at the uni accomodation also found it okay! Just a bit more basic than the private options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: This is where you need to have some patience with the university as it is quite difficult to find info about which courses are available to you. I needed to take master-level courses but if you are a bachelor student I would say it might be easier as there is just more courses to choose from. I had found courses I wanted to take but found out when I got to Stellenbosch that they were not available and/or overlapping, but 1-2 weeks into the exchange everything worked out fine and I got enough credits.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was exchange coordinators that helped loads! Just remember they have at least 100 exchange students each so they are not always able to reply asap.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At the end I got classes I was really satisfied with! I was quite open to different fields so there was not really a specific course I wanted to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not get too stressed if you do not know exactly which courses you are taking before getting there! Me and most of my friends all had to change some courses etc upon arrival but it all worked out for everyone in the end!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Quite similar to KU I would say, I took most of my courses in political science and found it really interesting! The level is quite similar, I would say maybe a bit easier grading-wise but a bit more work weekly (for example homework and/or presentations).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say it is quite similar, a mix between lecture and seminar style teachings where students are encouraged to participate.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Nature Cultures in Times of Plantatary Crisis
- Conflict in Africa
- Contemporary South African politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If possible I would recommend taking courses relating to South Africa, as it helps you understand the country you are staying in. I enjoyed contemporary south african politics although it was at times challenging as it was a master-level course for polisci students with a lot of prior knowledge of south african politics, but I learnt a lot!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: During my stay no unexpected costs, however the visa application cost more than I thought so good to keep that in mind.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is quite cheap which makes it easy to live as a student, for example uber and eating out is very affordable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not play any sports but my friends that did seemed really satisfied!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and sports! For example wine tasting society / scuba diving / running etc. basically anything you could imagine you could join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did volounteering through the university which I really enjoyed. There was plenty of different volounteering opportunites and they all got presented to us and then we could easily join whichever we wanted.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is so much to explore! If you enjoy hiking there is a lot of trails in and around Stellenbosch. There is also so many vineyards and a weekend activity was often going for a wine tasting (for less than 100DKK) at one of them! Cape Town is also only around 45mins way and is such an amazing city with lots to do! There are also a lot of opportunities for longer travel/holidays and I went to the Krueger park for safari which was really nice! There are also a lot of music events and festivals if that is your thing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy I would say! South Africans are super nice and welcoming people and that made it really easy to adjust. Just be open minded and you will have no issues.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was lucky to live with a South African and have a lot of neighbors that were South Africans which made it easy for me to get to know them, but there is also often a mix of exchange students and south africans in the classes which makes it very easy to get to know them! South Africans are really nice people and probably one of the easiest nationalities to befriend :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Not really a cultural difference but South Africa is a country with huge wealth inequalities and that is something you will see more than you are used to, which can be really hard. For example in Stellenbosch you will see quite a few homeless people and there is a township not to far away. Especially coming from Denmark this might be quite difficult to see. 

One less serious thing is that you will be forced to adapt to a slower pace of life, in South Africa there is very rarely a sense of urgency for anything, and I would recommend adapting to this pace or risk getting a bit annoyed over it, see it as an opportunity to slow down!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: South Africans are really happy people (in general) and it is not uncommon to see people dancing  or singing in the middle of the day for no reason.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Going into the exchange I was quite nervous about the satefy-aspect as it was something I had heard a lot about. Of course, you need to be much more vigilant than back home (not walk on our own at night, be careful with your phone etc especially in crowded places) but you get used to this quite quickly and I was never in a situation where I felt geniuenly unsafe! One big perk is that uber is extremely cheap and safe (also on your own) which makes it really easy to avoid unsafe situations such as walking alone at night.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, South Africa is an amazing country and Stellenbosch is a lovely town and university!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to create a life for yourself across the world is really cool, and probably the most rewarding part of the whole experience. Of course, it was hard at times but it was truly one of the coolest experiences of my life!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Of course it can be challenging to be far away in a different country, but I would just say to embrace the experience!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
